tiers.label: Light / cosmetic
tiers.scope: Paint, flooring, fixtures and minor cosmetic repairs. Assumes the structure and major systems work.

tiers.label: Moderate renovation
tiers.scope: Broader finishes, kitchen and bath updates, and selective system repairs. Scope is assumed, not observed.

tiers.label: Heavy / gut renovation
tiers.scope: Extensive demolition, systems and finishes. Does not price demolition and rebuilding a new house.

cost_source.name: HomeGuide national whole-house remodeling guide
cost_source.note: Published national bounds: whole-house remodeling $15–$60 per square foot; gut renovation $60–$150. The light/moderate split is our editable planning assumption, not measured High Point flipper cost.

flipper_context.name: ATTOM / Backflip Q1 2026 loan analysis
flipper_context.note: Charlotte funded-loan projects averaged a $58,857 construction budget in Q1 2026. This is historical flipper-budget context, not final invoices or a High Point average, and is not used as an individual property budget.

notes: Every scope is an assumed alternative. No scope is selected from tax bills, city cases, building age or old photographs.
Renovation rates use verified residential living area. Missing or ambiguous living area and unsupported building types remain unpriced.

Recorded county transfers are unreviewed sale-price benchmarks. The county feed does not publish an arm's-length flag or verified renovated condition. These are not appraisals or inspected after-repair values.
The same resale range is used across all repair scopes. Spending more does not automatically raise the resale estimate.
No future appreciation is assumed. Transfer-price quartiles describe the selected historical cohort, not a statistical prediction interval.
Other and financing costs default to an assumed $0 all-cash screening case. Enter actual financing and extraordinary costs before acting. Profit is before income tax.
Offer ceilings solve for the shared profit and return targets. They are not asking prices, offers accepted by owners, or evidence a property is available.
A negative offer ceiling means the scenario has no feasible nonnegative purchase price under these assumptions.
Contingency is applied once to the whole-house repair allowance. Do not add itemized kitchen, roof or systems costs already included in that allowance.
